query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Laboratory;
result: Patient has 1238 rows and 1238 distinct ID values. Examination has 806 rows and 763 distinct ID values. Laboratory has 13908 rows and 302 distinct ID values.
validation_method: read-only SQLite query against the source database; schema read with .schema confirmed Patient.ID is the declared primary key and Laboratory has a primary key over ID and Date while Examination declares no primary key

query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient); SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Laboratory WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Examination INTERSECT SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory); SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis>0 AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient); SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis>0 AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory);
result: Of 763 distinct Examination identifiers only 69 occur in Patient, leaving 700 examination rows unattached. All 302 distinct Laboratory identifiers occur in Patient. Only 20 identifiers are shared between Examination and Laboratory. Of the 75 patients with a thrombosis code greater than zero, 7 resolve to a Patient row and only 2 have any Laboratory rows.
validation_method: read-only SQLite set intersection between the ID columns of the three tables

query: SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis>0) t ON l.ID=t.ID;
result: The Laboratory table covers 302 distinct patients across 13908 rows, with a maximum of 226 rows for a single patient. Only 51 laboratory rows belong to patients with a thrombosis code greater than zero.
validation_method: read-only SQLite aggregation of row counts per identifier

query: SELECT Thrombosis, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY Thrombosis; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis>0;
result: Thrombosis equals 0 in 726 records, 1 in 57, 2 in 18 and 3 in 5, with no null values. 80 records carry a code greater than zero and they belong to 75 distinct patient identifiers.
validation_method: read-only SQLite value distribution and distinct-count check

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE (Symptoms IS NULL OR Symptoms='') AND Thrombosis=0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE (Symptoms IS NULL OR Symptoms='') AND Thrombosis>0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND Symptoms<>'' AND Thrombosis=0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND Symptoms<>'' AND Thrombosis>0;
result: 726 records have a blank Symptoms value and a thrombosis code of zero; 80 have a populated Symptoms value and a code greater than zero; the two discordant cells are both empty, so Symptoms is populated exactly when the thrombosis code is greater than zero.
validation_method: read-only SQLite contingency table between the two fields with all four cells enumerated

query: SELECT LAC, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY LAC; SELECT KCT, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY KCT; SELECT RVVT, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY RVVT;
result: LAC is blank in 584 records, '+' in 75 and '-' in 147. KCT is blank in 660, '+' in 41 and '-' in 105. RVVT is blank in 660, '+' in 47 and '-' in 99. No other values occur.
validation_method: read-only SQLite value distribution over the full examination table

query: SELECT LAC, KCT, RVVT, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY LAC,KCT,RVVT; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE KCT='+' OR RVVT='+'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE LAC='+' AND KCT='-' AND RVVT='-';
result: The largest groups are 584 records with all three blank and 88 with all three negative. 32 records are positive on all three. 17 records are LAC-positive with both assays blank, 15 are LAC-positive with KCT positive and RVVT blank, 9 are LAC-positive with KCT blank and RVVT positive and 2 are LAC-positive with both assays negative. 56 records have a positive KCT or RVVT while 75 are LAC-positive.
validation_method: read-only SQLite three-way contingency table over the full examination table

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE LAC='+' AND Thrombosis>0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE LAC='+' AND Thrombosis=0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE KCT='+' AND Thrombosis>0; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE RVVT='+' AND Thrombosis>0;

query: SELECT ANA, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY ANA ORDER BY ANA;

query: SELECT "ANA Pattern", COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY "ANA Pattern";
result: The field is blank in 261 records. Single patterns are P in 178, S in 252, N in 1, D in 1 and lower-case p in 2. Combined values appear as P,S in 89, S,P in 11, D,P in 2, D,S in 1, P,D in 1, D,P,S in 2, P,S with a period in 1, P.D in 1, S,D in 2, S,N in 1 and P, S in 1, so both the delimiter and the case vary between records.

query: SELECT MAX(length(Diagnosis)-length(replace(Diagnosis,',',''))) FROM Patient; SELECT DISTINCT trim(value) FROM Patient, json_each('["'||replace(Diagnosis,', ','","')||'"]') WHERE Diagnosis IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1;
result: The Patient table records up to three commas in one diagnosis value, so a row can hold up to four labels. Separators observed in the raw values include a comma, a caret-bracket sequence seen as RA followed by caret-bracket followed by SJS, and plain spaces as in the two-label forms joined by spaces. Distinct labels include SLE, SJS, RA, BEHCET, PSS, MCTD, APS and many uncertainty-suffixed variants such as SLE susp, RA susp. and MCTD susp, and spacing variants such as the same label written with one space and with two.
validation_method: read-only SQLite tokenisation of the comma-separated field plus raw value inspection

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Diagnosis IS NULL OR Diagnosis=''; SELECT DISTINCT trim(value) FROM Examination, json_each('["'||replace(Diagnosis,', ','","')||'"]') WHERE Diagnosis IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1;
result: The field is blank in 331 of 806 records and holds up to three commas in one value. Separators include a comma and a plus sign, as in SLE+pulmonary emboli+HLP. Distinct labels include SLE, SjS, RA, MCTD, PSS, APS, Behcet, brain infarction, thrombosis, DVT, pulmonary emboli and multiple thrombosis, alongside many uncertainty-suffixed and spacing variants.
validation_method: read-only SQLite tokenisation of the comma-separated field plus raw value inspection

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis GLOB '*SJS*'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis GLOB '*SjS*'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Diagnosis GLOB '*SjS*'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Diagnosis GLOB '*SJS*';
result: The Patient table contains the upper-case form SJS in 366 rows and the mixed-case form SjS in 0 rows. The Examination table contains SjS in 116 rows and SJS in 0 rows. The two tables therefore never share a spelling of this disease name, and the case-insensitive default of the LIKE operator conceals the divergence.
validation_method: read-only SQLite case-sensitive GLOB matching to separate the two spellings from the case-insensitive default

query: SELECT Diagnosis, COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Diagnosis LIKE '%thrombos%' OR Diagnosis LIKE '%emboli%' OR Diagnosis LIKE '%infarct%' OR Diagnosis LIKE '%DVT%' GROUP BY Diagnosis;
result: Thrombotic manifestations also appear inside the free-text diagnosis labels, including brain infarction on its own and combined with SjS, SLE and APS, thrombosis on its own, pulmonary emboli together with DVT, multiple thrombosis combined with SjS, spleen infarction combined with SLE, and the plus-joined form of SLE with pulmonary emboli and HLP.
validation_method: read-only SQLite free-text matching over the diagnosis label field
